independence_declaration.statement:
I am code-security-reviewer, session b527b36d-96b8-4ef0-b097-d8b61cf2659c, task T-DG7-REV-CS-RG4. I verified the assignment's SHA-256 (6e697fc5293fed3d2f98803358eff690717737e43d25a162b2257742585182e1).

I authored no implementation in the DG7 scope. The round-4 repairs were built by implementer roles: DO-D14 by devops-engineer and SA-ADR73 by solution-architect. delivery-orchestrator edited the drill script and ran the Compose drills (D-285).

I formed this verdict without opening any other reviewer's round-4 record or evidence. For F-DG7-1071 to F-DG7-1073 I read my own role's round-3 record and findings, and findings.json for the severities of earlier findings.

HEAD at the start was 08a9eb418, the round-4 freeze commit. It changes only the three round-4 assignments, candidates/DG7/9d3d5f62c921eb8f.manifest.json, stages.json and an orchestrator protocol-audit evidence file, all in META_EXCLUDES. The candidate id recomputes identically (SEC-RG4-00).

Two inconsistencies in the assignment are reported, not followed:
- It asks for `round: 7`, but the record path and the stages.json entry are round 4, and the validator requires rec.round to equal the round directory. This record says 4.
- It says candidate.mjs counts 3158 files. The tool and the frozen manifest both give 3160, and the id matches, so the count is stale.

I mirrored my role's DG7 round-3 record, which has the schema's full property set.

This review is engineering evidence only. It grants no business, Finance or IT approval. Product gate G6 does not imply DG7, and DG7 implies no G1-G6 approval.

checks_run.command: git rev-parse HEAD; git log --oneline 2fd69c37..HEAD; git diff --name-status 2fd69c37 HEAD; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG7; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG7 --ref 2fd69c3753ffb1f96aaf787f8526daa0bf59abe7; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG7 --ref HEAD; node tools/gates/candidate.mjs --stage DG7 --diff
checks_run.environment: Live repository, read-only; Node v24.21.0 (/opt/nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin first on PATH).
checks_run.expected: candidate sha256:9d3d5f62c921eb8f07ffb323b57d500a04e0608cbea2ed1ab0ebddec7b625403; the commits after the source commit change only metadata.
checks_run.actual:
HEAD is 08a9eb418, the round-4 freeze commit. It adds the three round-4 assignments, candidates/DG7/9d3d5f62c921eb8f.manifest.json and orchestrator/protocol-audit/protocol-audit-rg4.json, and modifies stages.json. All of these are META_EXCLUDES.

candidate.mjs gives sha256:9d3d5f62c921eb8f07ffb323b57d500a04e0608cbea2ed1ab0ebddec7b625403 over 3160 files for the working tree, --ref 2fd69c37 and --ref HEAD, all exit 0. --diff gives matches: true, with added, removed and changed all empty. The manifest has 3160 entries; the assignment's '3158' is stale.

I executed code only in a disposable `git clone --shared` sparse clone at 2fd69c37 under $TMPDIR. It excluded docs/delivery/{runs,test-evidence} and trading_agent/; handbacks/ was excluded at first and added later (see SEC-RG4-07). node_modules was symlinked to the repository's read-only install, except during SEC-RG4-11, where I used copies.

checks_run.command: for s in DG6 DG5 DG4 DG3 DG2 DG1 DG0; do node tools/gates/validate.mjs --historical --stage $s; done
checks_run.actual: 'PASS gate DGx (historical)', exit 0, for each of DG6, DG5, DG4, DG3, DG2, DG1 and DG0.

checks_run.procedure: Diff the round-3 source (3e8f5bce) against the round-4 source (2fd69c37) outside docs/delivery. Read every changed product file in full where it matters: backup.sh, restore.sh, compose-backup-drill.sh, the two tests, ADR-0066 and backup-restore.md. Confirm that no other product area changed.
checks_run.command: git diff --stat 3e8f5bce..2fd69c37 -- . ':!docs/delivery'; git diff --name-only 3e8f5bce..2fd69c37 -- tools apps packages licenses deploy/compose deploy/docker .github; git diff 389482803..2fd69c37 -- . ':!docs/delivery'
checks_run.expected: Only the DO-D14 / SA-ADR73 / D-285 files change; every change is correct and safe.

checks_run.procedure: Run the DO-D14-extended backup/restore suite on a disposable PostgreSQL in the clone.
checks_run.environment: Disposable clone at 2fd69c37; PostgreSQL 16.15 (UTF8, C) from tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh on port 32410; Node v24.21.0; shell uid 0 in a user namespace.
checks_run.expected: All tests pass. Any skip is explained.
checks_run.actual:
22 tests: 21 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped, exit 0. The pass list includes T-E11 (phased sequence: empty stderr, non-empty config.files equal to config/, digest, .backup-state removed), T-E11b (missing listing or changed config/: exit 1, no manifest), T-E14 (restored evidence owned by the root's owner, 0700/0600, R7 owner/otherOwner/groupOrOtherBits) and T-E14b (a non-numeric --evidence-owner is refused, exit 2, nothing written).

The skip is T-E14c ('as root, hand the evidence to uid 10001'). Its own probe `chown 10001:10001` fails with 'Invalid argument', because uid 10001 is not mapped in this sandbox's user namespace. The test skips with that reason, as designed. Its Compose equivalent ran in rg4c C8/C9 (SEC-RG4-04).

checks_run.procedure: Judge the orchestrator's Compose drill runs rg4, rg4b and rg4c (D-285; Docker is not available in my sandbox, so I did not re-run them): run.txt, the full drill logs, the restore report, the source/target evidence listings and finish.err. Compare the commits they ran with the candidate.
checks_run.command: cat compose-backup-rg4*/run.txt; read 02-compose-backup-drill.log; parse restore/restore-report.json; git diff 389482803..2fd69c37 -- . ':!docs/delivery'
checks_run.expected: A passing Compose drill on candidate content that moves real evidence objects and a job, reads the uid-10001 store under DAC_READ_SEARCH, and restores evidence owned by 10001 with 0700/0600. Failed runs are disclosed.
checks_run.actual:
rg4c: build exit 0, drill exit 0, C0-C11 PASS in 65.95 s on postgres:18 (pinned digest) and mth-app:local (sha256:7c4a85bf…).
- C2b: 2 objects uploaded, 10001:10001 0600.
- C4: 'copied 2 objects (2 distinct files, 146 bytes)'.
- C5: stderr noise 'none'; config.files has 3 entries; created jobs present.
- C6: the set is owner-only.
- C8: R1-R8 PASS. R7 = {verified 2, mismatches 0, owner 10001:10001, otherOwner 0, groupOrOtherBits 0}.
- C9: source and target have the same 2 files with the same SHA-256, read as uid 10001; 1 queued synthetic job.
- C10: /readyz 200 ready.
The only stderr in the log is Compose progress.

rg4 and rg4b: drill exit 1 at C2b, 'FAIL uploads: no transformation readable by the signed-in user'. The cause is the drill's seeding (dev users in their own organization), fixed by the D-285 edits. Later steps were NOT_RUN and recorded as such. Both runs are disclosed in D-285.

Provenance: rg4c's run.txt names 389482803, but the log shows the smoke.mjs step that was committed in 9b3547113. The product-path diff 389482803..2fd69c37 is exactly those 5 drill lines, and no image input changed. rg4b names b2864f2ab while already carrying the uncommitted seeding change. Neither affects the result.

This evidence closes F-DG7-1072 (see the verifications sidecar).

checks_run.procedure: Verify my three round-3 findings against this candidate's code, tests, Compose evidence, ADR-0066, D-285 and the allow-list citation. Record the results in the verifications sidecar.
checks_run.command: see SEC-RG4-02/03/04/10; grep -n 'D-285' tools/release/secret-allowlist.json docs/delivery/decisions.md; read ADR-0066 Amendment 2
checks_run.environment: Live repository, read-only, plus the clone runs cited.
checks_run.expected: Each repair holds on this candidate.
checks_run.actual:
F-DG7-1071 PASS: the listing is kept in .backup-state, checked in finish, and config.files is non-empty (T-E11, T-E11b, rg4c C5).
F-DG7-1072 PASS: the Compose drill moved 2 objects and 1 job, read the store under DAC_READ_SEARCH and restored it to 10001 0700/0600 (rg4c).
F-DG7-1073 PASS: ADR-0066 Amendment 2 records DO-D13 as built and answers Q2, and D-285 exists.
All three are CLOSED_VERIFIED in code-security-reviewer.verifications.json.

On the other open findings (comment only): F-DG7-1061/1081 are the same defect as 1071 and are repaired. F-DG7-1082 (Compose restore ownership) is repaired for the documented Compose volume path; the symlinked-root variant is F-DG7-1101. F-DG7-1083 is the same as 1073 for DO-D13.

checks_run.environment: Disposable clone at 2fd69c37, sparse with handbacks/; Node v24.21.0.
checks_run.actual: 14/14 pass, exit 0, including the two new 'Compose restore ownership (F-DG7-1072/1082)' tests.

checks_run.procedure: Adversarial probe of the new restore.sh ownership code: restore into a --target-evidence-path that is a symbolic link to an existing, empty 0700 directory. Control: the same probe with restore.sh of the round-3 source.
checks_run.command: cp backup-restore.test.mjs cs-probe-symlink.test.mjs (+ test CS-RG4-P1); QA_PG_PORT=32420 tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh node --test --test-name-pattern CS-RG4-P1 deploy/scripts/tests/cs-probe-symlink.test.mjs; control: git show 3e8f5bce:deploy/scripts/restore.sh > deploy/scripts/restore.sh, same command on port 32430, then git checkout restore.sh
checks_run.environment: Disposable clone at 2fd69c37; disposable PostgreSQL 16.15; uid 0 in a user namespace. The probe file was deleted from the clone afterwards; its copy is in the evidence.
checks_run.expected: A symlinked target root behaves like its target directory: exit 0 and R7 PASS, or a refusal before step 4.
checks_run.actual:
The probe exits 1 BY DESIGN (it asserts the expected behaviour). Its single assertion 'a symlinked evidence root is restored like a directory' fails with 1 !== 0.

restore.sh prints 'restore: check R7 failed: expected {... "groupOrOtherBits": 0}, got {... "groupOrOtherBits": 1}'. The target already holds 351 tables, and retention/ under the real directory is still 0755. Cause: stat/chown/find in restore.sh l.139/175-181/238-239 act on the link and not its target.

Control with the round-3 restore.sh: exit 0, all checks passed, R7 PASS. So this is a DO-D14 regression. Raised as F-DG7-1101 (Medium).

checks_run.procedure: Compare ADR-0066 (with its amendments) and backup-restore.md with DO-D14 as built and with the rg4c run, using the 'ADR claims enumerated and exactly true' rule applied in F-DG7-1041 and F-DG7-1073.

backup-restore.md l.227 still says the extended drill 'has not been run … recorded only when a run on a host with Docker exists'.

Both implementers flagged this (DO-D14 gap 4 and Q1/Q2; SA-ADR73 gap 3 and Q2), and D-285 does not dispose of it. Behaviour and tests are correct; this is documentation drift only. Raised as F-DG7-1102 (Low).

The guide's §5 ownership text and the §7 R7 row ARE updated and match restore.sh, apart from the symlink case of F-DG7-1101.

summary:
FAIL on sha256:9d3d5f62.

My three round-3 findings are CLOSED_VERIFIED:
- F-DG7-1071: the phased backup keeps the config listing in .backup-state; config.files is filled, finish refuses a missing listing or a changed config/, and stderr is clean (T-E11/T-E11b; rg4c C5).
- F-DG7-1072: Compose drill rg4c moved 2 real evidence objects and 1 queued job. It read the uid-10001 store under DAC_READ_SEARCH, and restore.sh handed the restored evidence to 10001 with 0700/0600, verified by hash as uid 10001. rg4 and rg4b failures are disclosed and explained.
- F-DG7-1073: ADR-0066 Amendment 2 records DO-D13, Q2 is answered, and D-285 exists.

The rest of the P7 surface is byte-identical to round 3. Historical gates DG0-DG6, the register, the unit suites, backup/restore (21 pass, 1 environment skip) and the secret and claims scans pass. The asset scan now passes on a faithful build and assembled runtime, which resolves my round-3 BLOCKED. Every artefact failure in my logs is explained and re-run.

Two new findings, none Critical, High or mandatory:
- F-DG7-1101 (Medium, devops-engineer): restore.sh's new ownership code acts on a symlinked --target-evidence-path itself and not on its target. The restore fails R7 (groupOrOtherBits 1) after the database is committed, and the default owner is taken from the link. Reproduced on PostgreSQL. The round-3 restore.sh passes the same case, so this is a DO-D14 regression.
- F-DG7-1102 (Low, solution-architect): ADR-0066 has no amendment for DO-D14, although A2.7 requires one. It still calls the shipped behaviour 'not behaviour' and states the old R7. backup-restore.md §8 still says the extended drill has no result.

A Medium must be repaired before the gate (D-192), so the verdict is FAIL.

This record grants no business, Finance or IT approval and does not imply DG7.
